name: exec_robot_create_thread
description:
Drives the robot along the path already generated for it by trace_targets. Returns immediately -- it posts the request and the tracking bench does the driving. Call wait_for_robot afterwards to find out how it ended.

Returns one of:
- "Started controller thread for robot <id>"
- "Path for specific robot doesn't exist. Generate path first"
- "No robot is attached to this service — start the bench with --rpc before asking anything to drive."
- "Selected ID doesn't exist (<ids>)"

robot_id.description: Robot ID. This rig has one robot and its id is 2.

robot_padding.description: Accepted and ignored. This rig has one robot, so there is nothing to keep clear of. Default: 30.

name: stop_robot_thread
description: Stops the robot. The bench disarms on its next tick and the ball coasts briefly to a halt.

robot_id.description: Robot ID whose drive should be stopped.

join_timeout.description: Accepted and ignored -- there is no thread to join. Default: 5.0.

name: wait_for_robot
description:
Waits for the current drive to finish and reports HOW it ended. Always call this after exec_robot_create_thread instead of polling get_robot_state, which wastes calls on round trips.

IMPORTANT: a robot stops for four different reasons and only one is success -- it arrived, it gave up stuck, the tracker lost the ball, or a person stopped it. Read 'arrived', not the fact that it stopped.

Returns {"arrived": bool, "outcome": str, "reason": str, "timed_out": bool}. When outcome is 'stuck' the ball is against a boundary; a goal further from the edge is worth trying. When outcome is 'refused' the rig would not start at all and 'reason' says why -- a mirrored camera frame or a missing calibration cannot be fixed by retrying.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait before giving up. Default: 30.

name: get_robot_position
description:
Where the tracker last saw the robot, in arena pixels.

Returns {"tracked": false, "reason": ...} when the ball is not currently visible -- a missing robot means 'not seen', never 'has not moved'. When tracked, 'theta' is the direction of TRAVEL rather than which way the robot faces (a Sphero is a sphere and has no visible facing); 'theta_is_measured' is false when the ball is at rest and the bearing is being held from its last motion, and 'theta_age_s' says how old that held bearing is.

name: get_robot_state
description: Returns 'moving' or 'halt'. Prefer wait_for_robot -- 'halt' says the robot stopped but not whether it arrived.
